what_happened: The job "Add plan/critic convention for content mirroring a governing source" (prompts) was rejected. The verifier marked 3 of 6 acceptance criteria unmet: (1) the test showing a plan fixture without the source list is rejected and the same fixture with it is accepted; (2) the planner and critic prompts stay within their 1300-token budgets; (3) no unrelated behavior changes, with cargo test, clippy and fmt all passing. It gave one major finding: the cargo test record for this candidate failed, and the verifier could not rerun it to clear it (the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR is cited). The one failed check was the test check. Its kept output is only CI cleanup lines (git config, orphan process cleanup, a Node.js 20 deprecation warning). No test name or assertion shows. The criteria all rest on cargo test, so the single unreadable test failure left all three unjudged. The failed check is not itself a criterion.
cause: Athena keeps the tail of the CI log as check output. That tail is post-job cleanup, so the failing test's name and assertion are cut off. The producer, the verifier and the the person running Athena therefore cannot tell whether the new test failed, a budget test failed (prompt edits to the planner and critic often break these, as in 20261027-170109-ycpz), or an unrelated test failed. The verifier cannot rerun the test in its shared target directory, so every criterion that depends on cargo test is marked unmet. Nothing extracts the failing test lines from the log or keeps them in the record.
prevention: When a test check fails, Athena should save the failing section of the log rather than its tail. That means the lines from "test result", "FAILED", "failures:" and "panicked at", with the test names and assertion messages. The save should also fall back to the full log if no such lines are found. The saved text should go into the check record, the rejection record and the producer's retry input. The record must never consist only of cleanup lines. This would let the producer and the the person running Athena see which test failed, and let the verifier judge each criterion separately.
proposed_request: Make a failed test check keep the output that shows what failed. Outcome: when the `cargo test` check fails in CI or locally, the check record stores the failing test names, the assertion or panic messages and the test summary lines, not the end of the log (cleanup and warnings). If no such lines are found, the record stores the full log up to a size cap and says so. The rejection event and the retry input for the producer include this text. Acceptance: (1) a test feeds a CI log whose end is only cleanup lines and whose middle has `failures:`, `panicked at` and `test result: FAILED` lines, and the stored output includes the failing test name and assertion message; (2) a log with no recognisable failure lines is stored in full up to the cap, with a note that no failure lines were found; (3) the rejection event for a failed test check shows the stored failing-test text; (4) `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Check the change against decisions in docs/decisions.md that cover check records and amend or confirm any it touches.
